input.quote: 11.2 Indemnification of AbbVie. Harpoon shall indemnify AbbVie, its Affiliates and its and their respective directors, officers, employees, and agents (the "AbbVie Indemnitees"), and defend and save each of them harmless, from and against any and all Losses in connection with any and all Third Party Claims incurred by or rendered against the AbbVie Indemnitees arising from or occurring as a result of: [***]
input.rationale:
Article 11's architecture is sound and partly favourable: Section 11.2 gives us an express defend-and-indemnify duty from Harpoon running to AbbVie, its Affiliates and their personnel for Third Party Claims, and Sections 11.3, 11.4.1 and 11.4.4 supply notice, control of the defence and cooperation. Those four preferred elements are already met and we leave them untouched.

The operative scope, however, is not established on the rendered record: both 11.2 and 11.1 end "arising from or occurring as a result of: [***]". Nothing rendered confirms that Harpoon's indemnity reaches third-party IP infringement, Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law, a Harpoon-caused data or confidentiality breach, or Harpoon's gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and nothing confirms that our own 11.1 exposure stays narrow. The Section 7.4 cross-reference ("Subject to Section 11.2") is inference, not operative indemnity text, and Section 7.4 otherwise puts first-line defence of third-party patent claims on AbbVie at its own expense. Fallback is also unavailable: the procure/modify/replace and refund remedies appear nowhere, and there is no 3x-annual-fees super-cap in Article 11.

We therefore add the missing scope as short additions to the existing trigger lists rather than rewriting them. Operation 2 confirms Harpoon's indemnity covers Third Party Claims alleging that the Licensed Compounds, Licensed Products, Harpoon Patents or Harpoon Know-How infringe or misappropriate Third Party intellectual property, plus Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law, Harpoon-caused unauthorized access to or disclosure of our Confidential Information or data, and Harpoon's gross negligence or willful misconduct. Operation 1 confines our 11.1 indemnity to AbbVie-provided materials, Information or content and AbbVie's breach of Applicable Law. Both are drafted as "without limiting"/limiting sentences so the redacted triggers are supplemented or capped rather than contradicted, and neither duplicates the 11.3/11.4 procedure. This is a scope-confirmation ask, not walk-away territory; if the unredacted triggers already carry this scope, the operations can be dropped.

proposal.summary: Add express IP-infringement, breach-of-law, data-breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct triggers to Harpoon's indemnity in 11.2, and confine AbbVie's 11.1 indemnity to AbbVie-provided materials and AbbVie's breach of Applicable Law.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Because the trigger lists in 11.1 and 11.2 are redacted, we add the scope our playbook requires as additions to the existing lists: Harpoon must indemnify and defend us for Third Party Claims alleging infringement or misappropriation of Third Party IP by the Licensed Compounds, Licensed Products, Harpoon Patents or Harpoon Know-How, and for Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law, Harpoon-caused unauthorized access to or disclosure of our Confidential Information or data, and Harpoon's gross negligence or willful misconduct. We also cap our own indemnity at AbbVie-provided materials and our breach of Applicable Law. The existing notice, control-of-defense and cooperation mechanics in 11.3 and 11.4 are untouched and continue to apply.

ops.text: AbbVie's indemnification and defense obligations under this Section 11.1 are limited to Third Party Claims arising from or occurring as a result of (a) materials, Information or content provided by AbbVie or its Affiliates hereunder and (b) AbbVie's breach of Applicable Law.

Without limiting the foregoing, the Third Party Claims for which Harpoon shall indemnify and defend the AbbVie Indemnitees under this Section 11.2 include those arising from or occurring as a result of: (a) any allegation that the Licensed Compounds, Licensed Products, Harpoon Patents or Harpoon Know-How infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right of a Third Party; (b) Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of AbbVie's Confidential Information or data caused by Harpoon; and (d) Harpoon's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
